output.name: Lethún

anatomy.part: head, crown of the gull's neck
breast, where the neck meets the body
body centre, the brightest star of the gull

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the gulls were nearest the knife and went first. One grey hen with a torn wing could not keep pace with the sky as it drifted, so she hung behind, crying. Tavo the Gale came down the coast laughing, as he does, and took her by the wing and turned her over like washing on the racks. Her wings went out stiff as sailcloth in a blow, and her body flattened thin as split cod. The Gulls heard her and carried her cry up to Mother Hesk at the pole. Tavo cannot be bargained with, so Hesk did not try. She counted every feather and wrote the count in the Spindle, so the gull would be held by the count if not by the string. Now she hangs over the Windward Reach, head up, tail down. My mother said to watch her when the wind is wrong. If she is still, the wind will hold. If she turns, bring the nets in.
output.verse:
Still gull on the wind,
wings out like wet sailcloth, held,
Hesk holds her in count.
